forecast.answer.title: Target {rps}: {answer}
forecast.chart.clipped_edge: Points beyond the chart edge ({count}) are triangles at the edge: during stalls and ramp-up, concurrency by Little's law shoots up.
forecast.chart.clipped_top: Values above the chart ({count}) are triangles at the top edge; exact numbers are in the tooltip.
forecast.chart.sla_above: The SLA p95 threshold ({value}) is above the chart.
forecast.chart.sla_no_p95: The SLA p95 threshold ({value}) is not shown: the forecast data has no p95.
forecast.chart.target_right: Target {rps} is to the right of the chart.
forecast.chart.zone_unstable: Red fill: the load at which stalls began in the test; the model is not built there.
forecast.chart.zone_untested: Fill: load above the tested range, where there is only a forecast.
forecast.confidence.basis_cpu: The estimate rests on measured steps: service CPU fits a straight line well.
forecast.confidence.basis_limit: The model fits the data well ({r2}): the {rps} limit is clearly visible.
forecast.confidence.basis_range: The target is within the tested range and the model fits the data well ({r2}).
forecast.confidence.label: Confidence: {level}
forecast.confluence.status_error: Could not check the Confluence publication (HTTP {status})
forecast.confluence.timeout: Publishing is taking too long, check the status later
forecast.controls.ceiling_hint: CPU load of one pod above which another pod is needed
forecast.controls.headroom_disabled: The limit is explained by service CPU: the pod CPU ceiling sets the headroom
forecast.controls.headroom_hint: Share of the limit to keep in reserve
forecast.explain.check_unverified: numbers not found in the data: {numbers}
forecast.explain.check_verified: numbers checked against the data: {matched} of {total}
forecast.explain.intro: AI will link the limit to the report findings below and assess the scaling risks. The numbers in its answer are checked against the data.
forecast.explain.no_findings: No report findings near the limit.
forecast.explain.title: Why it hit the limit
forecast.facts.instability: Stalls began at {time} ({label}, {rps}): {points}, mean up to {mean}.
forecast.facts.instability_p95: Stalls began at {time} ({label}, {rps}): {points}, mean up to {mean}, p95 up to {p95}.
forecast.facts.rps_drop: RPS dropped at {time}; later points are left out of the model.
forecast.facts.spikes: Isolated response time spikes: {count}, left out of the model.
forecast.latency.mean: Modelled response time at the target: mean ≈ {mean}.
forecast.latency.mean_p95: Modelled response time at the target: mean ≈ {mean}, p95 ≈ {p95}.
forecast.limit.instability: Limit {rps}: stalls began at this load in the test.
forecast.limit.model: Limit {rps}: the throughput ceiling of the model.
forecast.limit.none: The data shows no limit: RPS grows almost linearly across the tested range.
forecast.list.empty: There are no reports to forecast yet. A forecast is built for step and stress tests with a mean response time series.
forecast.list.hint.one: {n} more step or stress test has no forecast yet: {reasons}.
forecast.list.hint.other: {n} more step and stress tests have no forecast yet: {reasons}.
forecast.list.hint_missing_series: {count} — the data lacks the required series (add queries to “{domain}” and regenerate the report)
forecast.list.hint_missing_settings: {count} — the forecast settings are not set (SLA criteria → Capacity forecast)
forecast.list.subtitle: The capacity forecast uses the USL model and is built for maximum performance tests whose data has a mean response time series (and the number of VUs for a closed model). Choose a report.
forecast.list.title: Forecasting
forecast.method.all_included: All points of the window are in the model.
forecast.method.closed: Closed load model: concurrency is the number of VUs, think time in the scenario ≈ {seconds} s.
forecast.method.kappa: κ = {kappa}: the cost of keeping parallel requests coherent; because of κ, RPS falls after the peak.
forecast.method.kappa_zero: κ = 0: the model sees no RPS decline after the peak.
forecast.method.knee: Knee at {rps}: beyond it, response time grows faster than load.
forecast.method.no_knee: No knee before the limit: response time grows no faster than load.
forecast.method.open: Open load model: concurrency = RPS × mean response time.
forecast.method.pods: Pods: pod CPU = base + cost × RPS per pod, a straight line over the stable steps for each service. Pods needed = cost × target / (ceiling − base). Load is split evenly between pods, with the same request mix as in the test.
forecast.method.r2: R² = {r2}: the share of RPS variance the model explains.
forecast.method.sigma: σ = {sigma}: contention for a shared resource; the larger σ, the sooner RPS growth slows down.
forecast.method.usl_ceiling: Throughput ceiling by the USL model: {rps}.
forecast.method.usl_no_ceiling: The USL model shows no ceiling: RPS grows almost linearly across the tested range.
forecast.method.window: USL model (Universal Scalability Law) fitted to {points} of {minutes} min: from {start} to {end} ({reason}).
forecast.nodes.busiest: Nodes: the busiest at the target is {name} ≈ {cpu}, below the ceiling.
forecast.nodes.no_data: Nodes: no CPU data on the stable steps.
forecast.nodes.over: Nodes above the ceiling at the target: {nodes}; the added pods need room on other nodes.
forecast.page.subtitle: How much load the service can take, by a USL model fitted to the test steps.
forecast.page.title: Capacity forecast
forecast.plan.add: Add: {name} {from} → {to}, pod CPU at the target ≈ {after} instead of {current}.
forecast.plan.after_scaling: After that, CPU is enough up to {rps}; beyond it, {service} hits the limit first.
forecast.plan.blocked: The {rps} limit is not related to service CPU. Adding pods will not help: look for locks, connection pools, GC, external calls.
forecast.plan.blocked_busiest: The {rps} limit is not related to service CPU. At this load the busiest service is {service}, pod CPU ≈ {cpu}. Adding pods will not help: look for locks, connection pools, GC, external calls.
forecast.plan.busiest: Busiest: {name}, pod CPU at the target ≈ {cpu}, ceiling {ceiling}.
forecast.plan.cause_instability: Stalls from {rps} are explained by CPU: {service} at this load ≈ {cpu} per pod.
forecast.plan.cause_model: The model ceiling of {rps} is explained by CPU: {service} at this load ≈ {cpu} per pod.
forecast.plan.cpu_short: CPU will also run short: {name} at the target ≈ {cpu} needs {pods}, but that will not remove the limit.
forecast.plan.non_cpu_limit: Above {rps} it hits a limit not related to service CPU.
forecast.plan.stuck: {name}: pod CPU at zero load ≈ {base} is above the {ceiling} ceiling; more pods will not fix it: a higher CPU limit is needed.
forecast.plan.tight: Headroom to the limit is {pct}, {required} required.
forecast.plan.tight_not_cpu: Headroom to the limit is {pct}, {required} required: the limit is not related to service CPU.
forecast.reason.cpu_extrapolation: The target is {ratio} times the tested load: CPU is extrapolated along the straight line.
forecast.reason.cpu_fit: CPU of {services} does not fit a straight line well: the pod count is approximate.
forecast.reason.cpu_fit_action: Verify the pod count with a test.
forecast.reason.extrapolation: The target is outside the tested range: the forecast is an extrapolation.
forecast.reason.instability: Stalls do not fit a smooth model: above {rps} the forecast does not apply.
forecast.reason.instability_action: Investigate the stalls and rerun the steps around {rps}.
forecast.reason.instability_action_perio: Investigate the stalls (they recur about every {minutes} min) and rerun the steps around {rps}.
forecast.reason.low_r2: The model explains {share} of the data variance (R² = {r2}).
forecast.reason.low_r2_action: Rerun the test with longer steps: the points are widely scattered.
forecast.reason.scaling_untested: The test did not cover the configuration with the new pod count.
forecast.resources.note: Pod CPU ceiling {ceiling} ({source}); pod CPU is a straight line over {basis} without stalls.
forecast.resources.note_limit: ceiling {ceiling}: the test hit the limit at this CPU load
forecast.resources.note_poor_fit: CPU does not fit a straight line well
forecast.resources.rest.one: {n} more service stays at or below {cpu} pod CPU at the target.
forecast.resources.rest.other: {n} more services stay at or below {cpu} pod CPU at the target.
forecast.resources.title: Pods at {rps}
forecast.safe.cpu: Safe maximum of the current configuration: {rps}; beyond it, {service} goes above {cpu} CPU.
forecast.safe.headroom: Safe maximum with {pct} headroom to the limit: {rps}.
forecast.scale.caption_instability: Green zone: load with headroom; yellow: no headroom; red: stalls began at this load in the test. Hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
forecast.scale.caption_model: Green zone: load with headroom; yellow: no headroom; red: above the model ceiling. Hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
forecast.scale.caption_no_limit: Green bar: load the test passed without stalls; hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
forecast.scale.untested: Above the tested load: calculation only
forecast.scaling.no: Adding pods will not remove the cause
forecast.section.scale: Where the target sits on the load scale

forecast.unit.interval.title: Intervals
